title: Inky the octopus's great escape
hook: An octopus slipped out of his aquarium tank and found his own way to the sea.
peek: In 2016 the world heard how staff at New Zealand's National Aquarium had arrived one morning to find Inky the octopus gone. A gap in his tank lid, a trail across the floor and a drainpipe to the ocean told the story of a very neat escape.
lede: Inky was a common New Zealand octopus living at the National Aquarium of New Zealand in Napier. One night his tank lid was left slightly open after maintenance. Overnight he climbed out, crossed the floor and slipped into a drain that led to the sea. The story went around the world months later, in April 2016, and Inky was never seen again.

bullets.text: Inky had been caught in a crayfish pot by a local fisher and given to the aquarium. Staff described him as curious and clever, the kind of animal that liked to explore and play with things in his tank.

Staff worked out the route from the clues. Inky had squeezed through the small gap at the top of the tank, crossed a few metres of floor and found a drain hole leading to a pipe that runs out into Hawke's Bay.

An octopus has no bones. The only hard part of its body is its beak, so it can pass through almost any opening wider than that. Even a large octopus can squeeze through a gap only a few centimetres wide.
Octopuses are famous among keepers as escape artists, and many aquariums weigh down or latch their lids. Inky's story is unusual mainly because he seems to have made it all the way home.
